summary: This infographic explains how federally funded health centers (FQHCs) have accessibility obligations under Section 504, Section 1557, and the ADA, emphasizing the importance of telephone access for patient care. It presents evidence of multiple failed calls to JWCH-associated lines, contrasting with a successful control call, highlighting a documented accessibility concern and compliance questions.
full_text:
FQHC Accessibility Obligations → JWCH Telephone Access Evidence
How healthcare accessibility duties connect to the recorded phone-line failure

1) FQHC / federally funded health center
• Generally receives federal financial assistance
• Operates health programs and services
• Must provide equal, nondiscriminatory access

2) Accessibility requirements
Section 504
Disability nondiscrimination in programs receiving HHS funding
Section 1557
Health programs must provide meaningful and equal access; communications with people with disabilities must be as effective as with others
ADA
Parallel accessibility duties (Title III for private providers; Title II for public entities)

3) Why telephone access matters
• Scheduling lines, clinic lines, and patient communication are part of the pathway to care
• If these access points fail, patients may be blocked from reaching services
• A communication breakdown can become an accessibility barrier

4) JWCH evidence in the recording
1-866-733-5924 → Verizon Announcement 3 X Failed
1-562-867-7999 → Verizon Announcement 3 X Failed
661-942-2391 → Verizon Announcement 4 X Failed
Control call 1-248-434-5508 → Connected
Same handset, same recording sequence.

5) Recorded takeaway
The exhibit documents a time-stamped telephone access failure affecting JWCH-associated lines while a control call from the same handset successfully connected.
This creates a documented accessibility concern and raises compliance questions about access to care.

The recording shows the access barrier. It does not by itself establish the technical cause of the outage.
